newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RUGBY UNION-VETERAN CAMPESE SHINES ALONGSIDE STYLISH NEWCOMERS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-VETERAN CAMPESE SHINES ALONGSIDE STYLISH NEWCOMERS.

text.p: Australian veteran David Campese, making his final bow in world rugby, and a couple of international unknowns stole the plaudits on the opening day of the World Cup Sevens on Friday.
The day was essentially shadow boxing as the teams were ranked 1-24, based on results and tries, and redrawn into pools for Saturday's session.
Campese, playing his last tournament in an Australian shirt, saved the Wallabies from defeat in their opening game against Scotland and then orchestrated their 38-7 win over Romania.

The leading try scorer in international 15-a-side rugby with 64 in his 101 tests came on as a substitute with Australia, runners-up to England in the first World Cup Sevens in 1993, trailing 19-5 against Scotland.
He immediately turned things round, setting up and converting a try for Jim Williams which levelled the scores at 19-19.
"This is definitely the last time I play for Australia," Campese said. "I love playing in Hong Kong and I wanted to come as this is the World Cup.
"We have a very young side and we were a bit nervous to start. But at least we did not lose."
The Scots, meanwhile, who defeated the Romanians 26-14, took the wrappers off 20-year-old wing James Craig whose father Jim was in the Celtic soccer side which won the European Cup in 1967.
Craig junior has a personal best of 10.8 seconds for the 100 metres and showed his pace with three tries overall.

And favourites New Zealand, without key players Jonah Lomu and Christian Cullen, unleashed another force in the shape of Roger Randle who was influential in the tight 21-7 win over Tonga. New Zealand also beat Japan 47-14.
As luck would have it, New Zealand were drawn to play both sides again on Saturday.

England fly-half Mike Catt had the distinction of scoring the first try in the tournament as the holders made a competent start to the defence of the Melrose Cup, beating both Canada, 33-12, and Zimbabwe, 26-7.
"So far, so good," said England manager Andrew Harriman, who captained the winning side four years ago at Murrayfield.

Waisale Serevi, rated the best exponent of the sevens art, guided Fiji to a 59-0 win over Portugal and a 45-0 victory against hosts Hong Kong to ensure his side topped the rankings after the first day with 16 tries in their two wins.
